scenes.title: An assistant inside every screen
scenes.subtitle: It prepares the next step. You decide.
scenes.narration: The assistant reads incoming messages, prepares the next step and waits for your click. Here it takes one WhatsApp enquiry all the way to a booked trip.
A WhatsApp enquiry arrives. The assistant has already read it and pulled out the destinations, dates, travellers and budget.
One click on Create lead sets up the contact and the lead, with nothing typed, and the first follow-up is scheduled automatically.

lowerThird.feature: Contact and lead in one click

scenes.narration: It picks the closest itinerary template, and it drafts a first reply. You read the draft, change it if you like, and send.
Send the quote, and the lead moves to Proposal Sent by itself, with a follow-up two days later.

The customer replies: go ahead, and the advance is paid. The assistant offers to mark the lead won, creates the booking checklist, drafts the invoice, matches the payment with its bank reference, and drafts the hotel vouchers, a thank-you note and a request for the travellers' details.

lowerThird.feature: From a reply to a booking

scenes.narration: Everything the assistant suggested or did is on record, and most actions can be undone.
Each automation can be off, set to suggest, or automatic. Anything that sends a message or touches money always asks first, and one switch pauses them all.
Every morning the assistant looks for work: overdue invoices, quotes gone quiet or about to expire, balances due before travel, messages nobody answered, and rate cards running out.
And you can write your own rules: when something happens, check a condition, then suggest or do the next step.
Rule-based automations are free. AI features are switched on per feature and metered in credits, so you always see what has been used.

scenes.heading: From message to next step
scenes.narration: So the path is short: a message arrives, the assistant reads it, a suggestion appears, and one click puts it into action.
